A 38-year-old primigravida at 24 weeks' gestation presents with worsening colicky periumbilical and
epigastric pain over 3 days, along with fatigue and dysphagia that intensifies post-meals. She reports
morning red-colored urine since pain onset. Her prenatal care has been regular since week 8, with her
last visit being unremarkable. She takes only prenatal vitamins and denies substance use. Physical
examination reveals a temperature of 37.8°C, pulse 90/min, blood pressure 108/89 mm Hg, and
respirations 14/min. The fundal height is 6 cm above umbilicus, with abdominal distention and
tenderness in the epigastric and periumbilical regions, but no guarding or rebound. Imaging shows a
normal pregnancy with anterior placenta, no appendicitis or gallstones, and mesenteric vein
thrombosis. Cervical examination and fetal monitoring are reassuring. Laboratory findings show: |
**Laboratory test** | | | --- | --- | | Hemoglobin | 6.9 g/dL | | Platelets | 145,000/µL | | Leukocytes |
9,500/µL | | Reticulocyte count | 1% | | Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) | 800 U/L | | Mean corpuscular
volume (MCV) | 82 µm3 | | Haptoglobin | 25 mg/dL | | Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) | 37 | | Alanine
aminotransferase (ALT) | 43 | | Total bilirubin | 8.0 mg/dL | | Direct bilirubin | 2.5 mg/dL | | **Urinalysis** |
| | Color | Pink | | Glucose | Negative | | Protein | 3+ | | Hemosiderin | Positive | | Nitrite | Negative | |
Leukocyte esterase | Negative | | Bacteria | None | | Red blood cells (RBCs) | 2–3/hpf | | White blood
cells (WBCs) | 1/hpf | After initiating heparin and planning blood transfusion, what is the most
appropriate long-term management strategy for this patient's condition? Answer Choices: (A)

Anticoagulation therapy for life (B) Folic acid supplementation (C) Bone marrow transplant (D)
Corticosteroids (E) Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) (F) Iron supplementation with erythropoietin (G)
Plasmapheresis therapy (H) No further intervention necessary (I) Splenectomy (J) Eculizumab
administration
